Definition: a remainder or residual (surviving, final) portion
BiblicalUsage: The remnant is what is left after judgment, and Scripture will not let the story end there. The Simeonites smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, the Lord stirred up the spirit of all the remnant of the people to build, and the word comes to the remnant of Judah not to go down into Egypt. Zephaniah promises what the remnant will be: the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the remnant is God's answer to despair. He always keeps a people, and the people He keeps are the ones who turn back to Him. That is my hope for every generation that looks finished.
